bg.base.use: window background, the bottom layer; light theme is the iris paper

bg.surface.use: panes, cards, the HUD pill: the layer content sits on

bg.raised.use: inputs and secondary buttons at rest

bg.hover.use: a hovered control, row or list item

bg.selected.use: a selected row, list item or nav tab; the info banner (iris tint)

bg.warning.use: warning banner and low-confidence badge fill

bg.danger.use: error banner fill, a hovered destructive button

border.subtle.use: dividers, card outlines, a disabled input's outline

border.strong.use: button and container outlines, focused containers, the HUD outline

border.control.use: the edge of a field a person types into or picks from: text box, password box, combo box (WCAG 1.4.11, 3:1)

accent.primary.use: primary buttons, links (incl. "Open in Hudu"), focus ring, selection, info: Iris

text.on-accent.use: text on accent.primary; dark theme uses ink on the light iris tint

brand.signature.use: non-text brand iris: rules and marks at 3:1

brand.ribbon.band.use: the 4 px band over the selected row, the pill cap, the receipt rule; high contrast draws it in the window colour, so it is not seen

brand.ribbon.fold.use: one flat tone step where the band folds into the envelope (decorative, never the only cue); not seen in high contrast

state.scope.use: out-of-scope, excluded: slate teal (was violet #7442E0, ΔE 4.6 from Iris)

state.offline.use: offline / pending: v0.5 blue slate, unchanged

shell.bg.use: rail, title bar, pill: the frame (light: indigo navy #141030)

shell.muted.use: meta on the shell; control edges on the shell

shell.accent.use: focus and links on the shell

shell.scope.use: out of scope on the shell

contrast._note:
Every key in `color` must appear in text, backgrounds, indicators, structural, control_edges, a shell list, or in a `pairs` entry: ContrastTests enforces that, so a new token cannot be added without deciding what it is allowed to do.
  text: held to `minimum` against every background. state.danger is here as well as in indicators (v0.6.12): it draws words (the error line under a field, the Danger button's label), so it is held as text.
  backgrounds: every surface text or an indicator is ever drawn on, tints included (v0.5: hover, pressed, selected and the three banner fills), so a tint that dims the words fails here.
  indicators: held to `indicator_minimum`, WCAG's non-text bar, because Spec v0.4.2 confines them to a rule, a border, a dot or a glyph and never to body-size text.
  structural: dividers and container outlines. Held only to being a different colour from the background, not to 3:1. WCAG 1.4.11 applies to visuals that are the sole means of identifying a component or its state, and these are not: a control is identified by its own surface colour and its label, and the focus ring is accent.primary, which is in `text` and so held to 4.5:1.
  pairs: a colour that only ever meets one specific other. text.on-accent is unreadable on anything but the accent, and accent.primary.hover is never a surface for anything else, so they are checked against each other rather than against every background.
  control_edges: the edge that is the only thing showing where an input is (WCAG 1.4.11). An input's fill (bg.raised) is within 1.1:1 of the card it sits on, so its outline is what a person sees. Held to `control_edge_minimum` against every surface a control is placed on (`control_edge_backgrounds`): border.control outlines the text box, password box and combo box; text.muted outlines an unchecked check box and radio button; text.secondary draws the off toggle's track outline and thumb. Containers and cards keep border.strong, which is structural.
  shell_text, shell_indicators (v0.6.0): what is drawn on the frame (the rail, the title bar, the pill). Each is held against every entry in `shell_backgrounds`, text at `minimum` and indicators at `indicator_minimum`, the same bars as the content area.
  shell_structural: dividers on the frame, held only to being a different colour from it, as `structural` is for the content area.
  shell_decorative: brand colour that meets the frame only as decoration. brand.ribbon.band is an indicator on every content background (it sits on the selected row, 3:1), but where it meets shell.bg (the light pill cap) it is the logo case, iris on the frame at 2.80:1, deep by design. It is never the only cue there: the pill has its own outline and words, and high contrast does not show it. It is held only to being a different colour from the frame, and must stay in `indicators` so the content-area check still applies.
  brand.ribbon.fold is structural: a flat tone step, decorative, never the only cue.
  hc: the SystemColor each token maps to in client/ScreenTail.UI/Theme/Tokens.HighContrast.xaml, which is written by hand; HighContrastTokensTests holds the two together.
